title: cudaasync-slab-aging-and-long-tail-kv-retention-leading-to-gradual-rss-drift
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: After rolling out adaptive continuous batching + aggressive KV prefetching for long-lived conversational sessions, we've observed a slow, steady increase in GPU RSS over days on a subset of nodes. The pattern is not classic sudden leak (OOM) but a gradual drift that correlates with presence of long-tail (very long context) requests and low-weight background traffic. The goal of this ticket is to reproduce, narrow the root cause (allocator hysteresis vs slab aging vs retained KV view references), and implement short-term mitigations plus a long-term fix.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy runtime-1.20 w/ adaptive continuous batching enabled and KV prefetch set to conservative=off in staging pool
2) Start 50 simulated long-lived chat sessions that steadily append tokens so average sequence length per request grows over time (target 8k-30k tokens across the session lifetime),
3) Inject background mixed workload (short-gen 16-128 tokens) to exercise multipool allocator behavior and cross-stream caching
4) Monitor per-process GPU Resident Set Size (nvidia-smi, nvml counters), gpu-mempool stats, and kernel-level slab residency every 15m for 72+ hours

5) Collect CUDA allocator traces by enabling MALLOCASYNC_LOGGING and nvtx spans for batch boundaries, and capture KV cache reference counts and prefix hit/miss metrics from the runtime's tracing endpoint
observations: - RSS rises steadily (~200MB/day) on affected nodes; not correlated with steady throughput spikes; nodes never fully OOM but drift is reproducible in staging under the reproduce scenario.

- nvml reports resident pages increasing while per-request allocation histograms show no single large allocation that stays alive; rather many small allocations with delayed frees (deferred-free queues).
- cudaMallocAsync internal pool size (per-device) grows and shows long-lived arenas that don't get trimmed; pool trim heuristics appear not to trigger under low pressure.
- KV entries associated with 'active' sessions remain in cache; however some prefix slices show stale reference counts (refs > logical readers) after prefetch + eviction races.
- When we force a global KV cache compaction and call cudamempoolTrim (simulated via internal API), a portion of resident pages are released and RSS drops, but the growth resumes within hours.
- Timeline correlation: RSS growth accelerates after enabling batch-merging optimization that keeps more KV cache views pinned across calls to reduce latency for long sequences.
logs_and_artifacts: - link: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1284 (touched batching merge logic, for context)
hypothesis: 1) Allocator hysteresis: cudamallocAsync's pooling/arena retention heuristics combined with deferred frees (from async streams) accumulate when continuous batching merges streams and holds stream fences longer, preventing timely return of pages to device allocator.

2) KV view retention: aggressive batch-merge keeps KV view pointers alive across micro-batches; due to a subtle race, some views are not fully dereferenced on eviction and rely on finalizer path that runs on a different stream; finalizer stream lag leads to zombie references.

3) Slab/bitmap fragmentation: small prefix slices and mixed-size prefetches lead to fragmentation inside the allocator's arenas, causing the trim heuristics to believe memory is in use while actually fragmented and unreturnable.
4) Combined effect: none alone would cause sustained drift but together they produce a slow-resident growth that only trimming via heavy compaction clears temporarily.
proposed_changes: - 1) Add a periodic background compaction job (configurable; default 6h) that calls platform-level mempool trim and runs an explicit KV cache drain for entries older than configurable threshold.
- 2) Reduce the default batching merge hold time for sessions older than 48h to avoid pinning views across idle windows.
- 3) Instrument and export an 'allocations awaiting free' metric to detect deferred-free backlog sooner.
- 4) Update allocator integration to flush/advance finalizer streams when a threshold of deferred frees is reached, so pages can be returned sooner.
- 5) Fix KV cache eviction/refcount race discovered in runtime: ensure eviction marks entry as 'draining' and uses synchronous teardown path if draining takes longer than X ms.
- 6) Rework trim heuristics to consider fragmentation vs utilization (scan free block distribution in arenas before classifying as in-use).
testing_plan: - Unit tests for KV eviction path to assert refcounts go to zero under simulated prefetch+eviction interleavings.
- Add e2e load test that exercises very long sequences with continuous batching for 96h in staging and validates RSS slope < 10MB/day.
- Canary release: enable background compaction and reduced merge hold time on 10% of staging fleet; monitor replica-level RSS curves and error rates for 48h.
- Regression dashboard checks for CPU/GPU latency impacts from compaction and stream flushing; ensure tail latency not negatively impacted by aggressive trims.
rollout_plan: - Patch release runtime-1.20.1 with short-term mitigations behind feature flags.
- Roll to canary pool (10% nodes) for 48h; if stable and RSS slope reduced, roll to 50% then 100% over 3 days.
- After canary success, implement long-term runtime changes targeting runtime-1.21 with coordinated testing and a migration window for private deployments that need opt-in.
- Communicate to Dedicated customers about possible minor latency changes and offer toggle to disable periodic compaction if desired.
open_questions: - What is the real contribution of fragmentation vs deferred-free backlog? Need a micro-benchmark that isolates fragmentation effects.
- Are particular GPU SKUs showing worse behavior (A100 vs H100) due to different granularity of page management? Collect per-SKU traces.
- Could our batch-merge optimization be tuned to avoid holding KV views for sessions with low recent activity without regressing hot-client latency?
- Should we expose compaction and merge-hold configs to Dedicated customers as opt-in knobs?
